name: Joshua D. Jones
title: DevOps Engineer
tagline: Secure delivery, hardened containers, and observable Kubernetes.
summary: I build and ship software into secure environments: distroless images, GitOps pipelines, and Kubernetes clusters that are hardened by default and observable from day one.
Currently a DevOps Engineer at KBR, finishing an M.Eng. in Cybersecurity at UCCS, and preparing for the CKA.

points: Build distroless container images to minimize attack surface and reduce vulnerability findings.
Research and remediate allowlisted vulnerabilities, eliminating accepted-risk exceptions in scans.
Maintain GitLab CI pipelines and deploy software across environments with Zarf and Zarf Bundles for releases into secure environments.
Troubleshoot Kubernetes pod and deployment failures from logs and cluster events to fix configuration errors that block rollouts.
Built multi-branch GitHub Actions CI/CD pipelines (flake8, pytest, CodeQL, Trivy) publishing images to Nexus, with continuous delivery to Kubernetes via Argo CD.
Configured a three-node Talos Linux Kubernetes cluster from scratch, including CNI, VIP, and etcd.
Deployed apps with Gateway API (HTTPRoute/GRPCRoute) under the PodSecurity restricted policy, and managed ARC scale sets for self-hosted runners.
Implemented monitoring with kube-prometheus-stack and Grafana, using Thanos and MinIO to consolidate metrics from three clusters into one dashboard with long-term retention.

experience.org: OIT, University of Colorado, Colorado Springs
points: Provided Tier 3 support for campus network connectivity issues.
Installed and configured Cisco switches and Aruba APs; terminated, tested, and labeled cabling.
Maintained network documentation, topology diagrams, and knowledge base articles.

points: Provided Tier 1 and 2 support across Windows, macOS, and virtual machines.
Administered Active Directory, Exchange, Jamf, network printing, and VMware VM deployments.
